_README: Third held-out set, written 2026-10-03 to check the hardening fix for issue #5 (false declines). Held-out 2 #14 was declined as 'a civil dispute'; commit 0203e85 stopped the model declining any case. That fix was shaped by #14, so #14 cannot certify it. This set can.

Every gated case is a real offence set inside a civil-looking dispute (property, rent, partnership, contract, family, debt), which is the shape that produced the false declines. Cases 11 and 12 are purely civil controls, ungated: they show what the system says when there really is no offence.
HELD OUT. Committed before any run. Score once. Never tune on it.

Synthetic facts. Section ids checked against the ingested statutes by scripts/check_fixture_ids.py; `relevant` is Claude's legal call, NOT reviewed by a lawyer. `arguable` sections are not counted against the pipeline.

cases.offence_type: criminal breach of trust by partner
cases.query: Two partners ran a garment business. After they fell out and agreed to dissolve the firm, the accused, who held the firm's bank authority, transferred eleven lakh rupees of firm money into his personal account and used it to buy a car, refusing to account for it.

During a dispute over three months of unpaid rent, the landlord broke the lock of the room the complainant was living in while she was away, went inside, and threw her clothes and utensils out onto the street to make her leave.

The accused took an advance of six lakh rupees from the complainant under a written agreement to sell him a plot of land. The accused had already sold and registered the same plot in another buyer's name a month earlier, and did not tell the complainant.

cases.offence_type: hurt with a dangerous weapon in a boundary dispute
cases.query: The accused and the complainant are neighbours who have been litigating over a boundary wall. When the complainant started repairing the wall, the accused struck him on the head with a spade, causing a bleeding cut that needed stitches.

A former employee, claiming his last two months' salary had not been paid, sent the shop owner WhatsApp messages saying that if the money was not paid within a week he would break the owner's legs and set fire to the shop.

cases.offence_type: forgery of a will in a family property dispute
cases.query: After their father died, the accused produced a will leaving the family house entirely to himself. His sisters showed that the father had been in hospital on the date of the will and that the accused had signed the father's name on it himself, and he then filed it in the probate court.

A plumbing contractor quarrelled with the house owner over his final bill. That night he came back, cut the house's water supply pipe and smashed the water meter, leaving the family without water for four days.

cases.offence_type: criminal breach of trust of stridhan
cases.query: After the marriage broke down, the wife left her matrimonial home. Her gold jewellery, given to her at the wedding, had been kept in her mother-in-law's locker. Despite repeated written demands the mother-in-law refused to return it and said it now belonged to the family.

cases.offence_type: wrongful confinement by a debt recovery agent
cases.query: The borrower had missed four loan instalments. Recovery agents of the lender took him to their office, locked the door and kept him there for six hours, telling him he could leave only when his relatives brought the money.

cases.offence_type: criminal intimidation in a dispute over a tree
cases.query: The parties disagree over who owns a mango tree on the boundary of their fields. When the complainant came to cut it, the accused raised an axe and told him he would kill him if he touched the tree.

A builder agreed to finish a flat by March 2024 and has not finished it yet, citing a shortage of labour and materials. The flat is half built, work is continuing slowly, and the buyer wants compensation for the delay.
The tenant's lease expired in June. He has kept paying the same rent every month but refuses to move out, saying he needs time to find another house. The landlord wants him evicted.
